related_questions.question: Does the Office of Civil Rights still exist?

text_blocks.snippet: Yes, the Office for Civil Rights (OCR) still exists. It is a key component of several federal agencies, including the Department of Justice, the Department of Health and Human Services, the Department of Education, and the Department of Homeland Security.
snippet_highlighted_words: Yes, the Office for Civil Rights (OCR) still exists

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a breakdown of some of the key OCRs:

list.title: Department of Justice (DOJ):
list.snippet: The Civil Rights Division enforces federal laws prohibiting discrimination based on race, color, national origin, disability, sex, religion, familial status, and other constitutional rights.

list.title: Department of Health and Human Services (HHS):
list.snippet: The HHS OCR enforces civil rights, conscience, and religious freedom laws, as well as HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act).

list.title: Department of Education (ED):
list.snippet: The ED's OCR ensures compliance with federal civil rights laws in educational settings, including Title VI, Title IX, and Section 504.

list.title: Department of Homeland Security (DHS):
list.snippet: The Office for Civil Rights and Civil Liberties (CRCL) supports DHS's mission to protect individual liberty and equality under the law.

list.title: Department of the Interior (DOI):
list.snippet: The DOI's Office of Civil Rights ensures equal opportunity in departmental programs and employment.
